biggestGap: Nothing in the game consumes it. There is no ship-height query, no LOD past the single patch, and no setCenter caller. The surface is real and measured, but maritime travel cannot yet stand a ship on it. Until it does, this is a proven capability sitting beside the game rather than in it.
notes:
THREE CASCADES. The third is a 13 m ripple patch at a 0.051 m texel, and it fixes the water-level read: at 1.6 m eye height the two-cascade sea was a smooth teal hill, and the three-cascade sea has breaking crests, foam streaks and fine texture to the horizon. Compare round-1-water-level-2cascade against round-1-water-level.

It is a SPLIT, not an addition. The wind-sea low cutoff moved 0 -> 13 m carrying the same JONSWAP spectrum. Energy moved; it did not appear. Conserved to 2.0%, Hs held 11.96 vs 11.99 ft. Patches 13/97/1291 are all prime, so the repeat period went 125 km -> 1,629 km.

CAUGHT BY MEASUREMENT, not by eye: the split stripped the wind sea of the short steep waves doing the folding, and foam coverage fell 4.25% -> 0.38%. Fixed by combining the ripple and wind-sea Jacobians through their deficits, validated against the exact determinant of the summed gradient (RMS error 0.010).

STRONGEST GATE IN THE CAMPAIGN: the whole pipeline is written twice, once in TSL and once in plain TypeScript with a naive DFT oracle. GPU vs CPU max absolute error 1.29-2.96 um, relative RMS 9.1e-7 to 3.6e-6. 60 tests assert real spectral identities, not that it looks wavy.

Perf: draw 0.51 -> 0.75 ms. Compute was NOT claimed - the measurements did not order correctly across sessions, so no delta was reported.

The standalone harness misc/ocean.html is RETIRED. Everything it had lives at ?step=water&ocean=1, including camera presets, five debug channels, and the bench/hash/crossCheck probes.
